question:
At the end of each release our bug tracker tells us only how many bugs were found, and that count gives the team nothing to act on. What should we do with our bug records so that they help us introduce fewer bugs in later releases?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Bug counts alone are insufficient to drive improvement. Teams should classify defects by type, perform root cause analysis, build defect profiles, apply statistical and trend analysis, record findings, and implement corrective/preventive actions so that measurement data actively guides future process and product quality improvement.

# Guidelines

- Classify bugs by type and category, not just count them; numbers alone without classification are insufficient to identify underlying causes and prevent recurrence. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt 6caeafab158e568bb914] anomalies, and ensure [SWEBOK excerpt 18d6512e7355e8c13362] are recorded rather than lost. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Perform root cause analysis (RCA) to find root causes of defects and use measurement techniques to improve software engineering processes, techniques, and tools. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Develop defect profiles for the specific application domain; for the next project, use those profiles to focus SQM [SWEBOK excerpt 77c7a6c83a6846f86d06], and use defect density and failure rate data to support software process improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Software Quality Measurements and Reliability Models.md)

- Use RCA techniques such as 5-whys, cause-and-effect (Ishikawa) diagrams, change analysis, and fault tree analysis to isolate the root cause of recurring defects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Root Cause Analysis Techniques.md)

- Apply Pareto analysis and frequency-severity prioritization to select the highest-priority defect problems to address, gather evidence about their causes, then select and implement corrective actions that prevent recurrence. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Root Cause Analysis in Process Improvement.md)

- Select corrective actions that prevent recurrence, are within the organization's control, meet organizational goals, and do not cause other problems; then observe those actions to ensure their efficiency and effectiveness. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Industry 4.0 and Software Engineering Integration.md)

- Document corrective and preventive actions and submit them so the quality management system is improved and problems are prevented from recurring in future projects; use an independent organization to monitor progress and inform stakeholders. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- Apply descriptive statistics, trend analysis, and control charts to identify the most troublesome defect areas, detect when certain classes of faults are becoming more likely, and focus process improvement resources accordingly. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Measurement and Analysis Techniques/Software Quality Measurement and Statistical Analysis Techniques.md)

- Record test incidents in a problem reporting system with full context (when, who, configuration) so they form a basis for debugging, fixing, and identifying which aspects of the software testing and development process need improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Test Generation, Environment Setup, and Incident Management/Test Incident Reporting and Documentation Process.md)

- Use fault type classification and statistics, including the relative frequency with which fault types have occurred in the past, to make quality predictions and drive process improvement in future projects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/SUT Measurements and Fault Classification for Test Planning.md)

- Use history of faults discovered in earlier projects as a primary input to error-guessing test design, so that the most plausible faults in each new system are specifically targeted. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Software Testing Techniques and Methodologies/Experience-Based Techniques for Test Suite Generation.md)

- Combine evaluation of test phase reports [SWEBOK excerpt 9fb7323e3690f612d29a]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Test Management and Process Monitoring/Test Team Organization and Process Measures.md)

- Feed lessons learned from defect data into the organization's measurement database and conduct retrospective analysis so that issues encountered can be analyzed and fed into organizational learning and improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)

- Ensure every metric collected is linked to a decision; avoid gathering defect measurements merely because they are easy to collect—those that do not support any decision are a waste of time and energy. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Measurement Scales, Reliability, and Practical Application/Measurement Reliability and Decision-Driven Metrics/Measurement Purpose and Avoiding Wasteful Metrics.md)
